findings.problem: A browser_lock intent recorded before keeper spawn could be borrowed as though an apply keeper existed, permanently holding a rollback on a missing held receipt.
findings.correction: Only invocation_may_have_started is eligible for borrowing. intent_saved/precondition_failed create a separate rollback acquisition; unknown phase is denied. Invoked/uncertain acquisition remains readback-only.
findings.verification: review-rollback-correction-1795351813.json/.log: four tests passed, including both proven-unissued phases and retained invoked/unknown-signal cases.

reviewed_invariants: Manifest remains UNBOUND; exact root-reviewed live binding and authorization are mandatory before preflight or activation.
Existing root-owned global release lock, active operator lease, seven preserved process identities, exact source/dependency pins and eleven verified backup/restore receipts precede actions.
Core maintenance close/open uses the existing fixed service-owner CLI with an explicit distinct operator actor, exact epoch/command receipts and durable invocation phase.
Only an exact owned IPv4 nft table blocks new nonroot SYNs to 127.0.0.1:8810. Established sessions are not reset; complete preexisting firewall metadata and owned handles are pinned.
The actual application shared lock is held by a fixed verified root keeper. It survives disconnected operators and does not remove a replacement owner lock.

Before the one pidfd SIGTERM, the bootstrap waits naturally for no usable ingress or Node-owned network sockets beyond the bound Hermes header wait, then requires fresh health/active-turn proof, terminal legacy ERP/development journals, empty current Core admissions and unchanged historical full-row digests.

The root-only health probe is explicitly allowed to expire only the derived empty project catalog. It backs up original cache bytes, validates exact timestamp/shape, and rechecks authoritative state and target inventory.

Only the exact Node identity receives a single recorded SIGTERM. Unknown signal/command outcomes are reconciled through original receipts and process identity; no forced termination, duplicate signal, whole-unit restart or historical-job settlement.
The successor must have the pinned runtime identity, unchanged watchdog parent, correct listener and required start ordering; the first verified successor is recorded and cannot silently be replaced.
Source rollback restores only the three known leaves/absence preimages. It cannot reset data, remove foreign source, replay an uncertain Node signal, or signal an unobserved watchdog recovery.
New relay shutdown owns handler promises, scoped turns, ERP turns and ERP inspections until completion, including client disconnects; no new requests or delayed reservations are admitted after drain.

Restored-target diagnostic retains primary authorization, exact Core observe proof, original root/account/envelope identity and final revalidation; it returns only bounded fixed metadata and never navigates, sends, binds, captures or declares safe replay.

verification.operator_coverage_note: 25 baseline methods, two successor methods, one new rollback method; changed rollback group rerun four methods on final hash. Unchanged broad suites were not rerun by reviewer.

limitations: Source acceptance only. This reviewer did not bind an activation manifest, stage private operator files, change the host firewall, signal a live process or execute provider/browser work.

Whole operator sequencing uses finite fixtures; real pidfd, shared-lock and private-network-namespace tests cover bounded components. Full production activation remains a separate fresh preflight and observed operation.

The normal-identity live-dependency hash sweep stopped on permission denied for /srv/abit-dev-linux/relay-runtime/service/agentic-gateway/relay.cjs. No alternate identity or bypass was attempted. The package carries 23 dependency pins, and the authorized root preflight must verify the complete current live closure.
Intentionally uncertain external commands remain held if their exact outcome cannot be proved. Source acceptance does not authorize guessing, clearing old journals or repeating those commands.
The private namespace test proves the narrow nft rule in a distinct kernel network namespace; it does not claim a host firewall action already occurred.
